result.title: Which and When to Admit: Gradient Admission for Data-Centric Small Language Model Finetuning
result.summary: LoRA fine-tuning adapts small language models (SLMs) to heterogeneous instruction data within a low-rank update subspace, making it vulnerable to three structural problems: conflicting gradients that cancel, static data selection that cannot track evolving learning dynamics, and subspace saturation that causes later updates to overwrite useful directions. We argue that effective adaptation therefore requires controlling which data-induced gradients enter the LoRA subspace and when. We propose GRADE (GRadient-Aligned Data-centric rEcipe), a data-centric framework combining two mechanisms: a state-aware selector that continually admits samples aligned with the evolving multi-task gradient field, and a self-calibrating step-level gate that rejects updates likely to cause destructive overwrite near saturation. Across three current-generation backbones and a heterogeneous seven-dataset instruction pool, GRADE outperforms strong data-selection and PEFT-stabilization baselines in accuracy and robustness. It is the only method to improve consistently over standard LoRA on every architecture, while producing more coherent gradient trajectories and less destructive overwrite. These results show that successful SLM adaptation depends not only on which data are selected, but also on which gradients are allowed to enter and persist in the constrained update subspace.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文面向小语言模型的 LoRA 指令微调，提出 GRADE 框架：用状态感知的数据选择器持续接纳与演化中多任务梯度场对齐的样本，并用步级门控拒绝接近子空间饱和时可能造成破坏性覆盖的更新。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「何时接纳哪个梯度进入受限更新子空间」的思路，可能与 LVR 中推理状态何时写入、如何避免有用方向被覆盖及贡献分配问题相关，可供核查；但论文限于文本 LoRA 训练，无视觉或多模态推理验证，迁移属推测。
